rv.q: The performances are solid and there's an impressively lush set by Robert Innes Hopkins — complete with pools of dirty water for the cast to splash around in.
Firth makes some sharp points about male insufficiency but I get the sense of a good 90-minute idea being stretched to fill the requisite two-act running time.

cn.t: Tim Firth's 20-year-old comedy about stranded colleagues features solid performances from its quartet, but the descent into savagery stretches credulity and three of the four characters prove unsympathetic.
